idea-plugin.name: Octopus Merge
idea-plugin.description:
Merge several Git branches into one with a single merge commit (an octopus merge), with a conflict preview and conflict resolution in the regular IDE merge dialog.

Where to find it

  • Git | Octopus Merge…, right below Merge…
  • The octopus button on the main toolbar, on the branches toolbar of the Git tool window (⌘9 / Alt+9) and in the branch popup
  • Right-click selected branches or commits in the Git tool window: they come pre-checked
  • Find Action: type Octopus

How to use

  1. Merge into: type or pick the target branch.
  2. Check the branches to merge; the search field filters by every typed word.
  3. Arrange the Merge order with ↑/↓. Each branch shows what will happen: ✓ commits it brings, ⚠ expected conflicts and their files, or already merged. The preview never touches your working tree.
  4. Double-click a branch with ⚠ to resolve its conflicts right away, before merging.
  5. Edit the message if needed and press Merge.

Conflicts

Resolve in advance. Double-click a conflicting branch in Merge order (or press Enter): the regular three-way merge window opens on in-memory copies, with the target plus every branch merged before it on the left. The branch turns ✓ resolved in advance, later branches are predicted against your result, and the merge applies it without stopping. A resolution is used only for the exact conflict it was made for: change the order or update a branch and you are simply asked again.

Plain git merge refuses an octopus merge as soon as anything conflicts. This plugin merges the branches one by one instead and opens the standard Conflicts dialog for every conflicting branch. Afterwards the intermediate commits are replaced by one commit whose parents are the target and every merged branch: the history looks exactly like an octopus merge. Cancel at any point and everything is rolled back. Or let git decide with -X ours / -X theirs.

Options

  • Stash local changes and restore them afterwards
  • --no-commit: stage the result and commit it yourself, still as an octopus merge
  • --log, --signoff, -S (GPG), --no-verify, --allow-unrelated-histories
  • Delete merged local branches

After the merge, the notification offers Undo: the target returns to its previous commit and deleted branches are recreated.
